description: The Performance Assessment System (PAS) is an online performance measurement and monitoring system for urban water supply and sanitation in India, produced by CEPT University from 2008 with partner institutes and state governments and hosted on www.pas.org.in (built with Tata Consultancy Services). It holds annual service level benchmark indicators entered by urban local bodies for four sectors (water supply, wastewater management, solid waste management and storm water drainage), with equity and local action indicators and a reliability grade for each indicator. Coverage, as given in the 2018 executive summary on the portal: more than 900 cities in six states (Gujarat, Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Jharkhand and Assam), a continuous series for more than 400 cities in Gujarat and Maharashtra, and three years of indicators for over 1,800 cities in 18 states. Access is free and open on the portal through city profiles, interactive dashboards and reports; no licence is stated. Caveats: the indicators are self-reported by the cities, the portal's pages are generated by scripts and could not be read from the cloud session (only its PDF documents), and the coverage figures date from 2018. Simulation uses: city-level service levels, non-revenue water and cost recovery for capacity planning and for setting baselines of urban water service resilience. Related records: the Australian national performance report for urban water (data-bom-national-performance-report-urban-water).
